facts.fact: The education sector plan's mid-term review (Jimma University, 2019), as tabulated in this UNESCO case study, gives 592 as the performance against a 2017-2018 target of all for the number of woreda offices with relevant infrastructure using the Integrated Financial Management Information System to record transactions; the study does not say how those offices are connected, and gives no total of woredas.

592 woreda offices with relevant infrastructure were using IFMIS to record transactions against a 2017-2018 target of all woreda offices, on the education sector plan's mid-term review (Jimma University, 2019) as tabulated by the UNESCO case study; no denominator is given.

The UNESCO case study, from interviews and a visit to Gambella around 2019, states that the annual school census moves on paper: three-copy questionnaires are carried between schools and woredas, sometimes on foot, woredas stamp them and send them to regional education bureaus often by public transport, data entry is done at the bureaus, and more often than not there are no computers at woreda level.
